goal: Explain one original lounge-chair concept through a clear industrial-design development board without presenting generated ideas as validated engineering.
audience: Industrial-design reviewers comparing form evolution, concept views, structure intent, and material direction

content.subject: One original faceted lounge-chair concept shown through five coherent stages on a vertical industrial-design development board
must_include: One consistent original faceted lounge-chair identity
Front, side, and top concept views without measurements
A conceptual internal frame and two restrained material directions
must_avoid: Dimensions, seating angles, tolerances, or anthropometric numbers
Blueprint, patent, construction, validation, or certification claims
Pseudo-text, extra labels, brands, logos, signatures, or watermarks
Copied real products or recognisable portfolio work

art_direction.style: Premium industrial-design portfolio board combining photorealistic clay-model renders, graphite concept drawings, and restrained editorial layout
art_direction.lighting: Soft neutral studio light with quiet museum-catalogue precision

composition.layout: Portrait modular board with a large upper-right hero, compact upper-left studies, one ordered evolution strip, concept views, a structure-and-material row, and a final detail row
composition.viewpoint: Consistent three-quarter product views supported by clean front, side, and top concept views

references.notes: Project-created edit target and sole visual authority for the original faceted chair identity and five-stage board concept; not distributed as an approved public asset.

objective_checks: Output is exactly 972x1619 PNG/RGB without alpha
Every specified text string appears exactly once
No other visible words, numerals, dimensions, logo, brand, signature, or watermark appears
visual_checks: The faceted arm geometry, tall folded back, inset cushion, and stable base remain coherent across every process view
The five stages read in order with clear hierarchy, generous spacing, and no illegible body copy
The conceptual internal frame visually fits the shell but does not imply validated construction documentation
Mineral shell, woven textile, tubular frame, paper, and shadows remain materially credible
The result is visibly distinct from a product advertisement, exploded product diagram, or engineering blueprint
